headline: Two and a half days in *Hanoi*.
footer: With Os’s parents, then Bangkok together.

paragraphs: The end of Os’s fortnight in Vietnam with family, and the start of ours. Jabari arrives on the 13th, and for two and a half days it is the four of us in the Old Quarter.
No day trips, because there is no time for them. Everything below is walkable or a short ride, and nothing on this page is booked.

notes.lead: Four of us, so a gentle pace.
notes.rest: Mornings for the sights, afternoons slow, and the evenings for eating.
One car to Noi Bai for all four of us. The morning still has room for the Temple of Literature or a last coffee.
The walking street round the lake and the weekend night market both run Friday to Sunday, so they miss us.
Around 29°C by day and 22°C at night, short showers on some days, and sunset at about 17:30.

sections.title: The days
sections.note: One rough shape, easy to ignore.

items.name: Jabari arrives
items.detail: The lake at dusk, egg coffee, and the 17:20 water puppets if everyone has the energy.

items.name: The full day
items.detail: West Lake or the Temple of Literature in the morning, a slow afternoon, Long Biên at sunset, and the street food walk at 17:00 or 18:30.

items.name: Out at 15:30
items.detail: A last morning in the Old Quarter, then the car to the airport. Os’s parents fly home to Barcelona, and the two of us fly to Bangkok.

sections.title: If there is time

items.name: Hoa Lo Prison
items.detail: The colonial prison later known as the Hanoi Hilton. Sobering, and an hour or so is enough. The night tours only run on weekends.

items.name: Museum of Ethnology
items.detail: The best museum in the city, with full-size village houses outside that suit all ages. Half a day, closed Mondays.

items.name: A cooking class
items.detail: Rose Kitchen starts with a market visit and picks up in the Old Quarter. A good half-day for four.

items.name: GC Bar
items.detail: Hanoi’s longest-running gay bar, relaxed on a weeknight, with a pool table.

sections.caveat: Prices and hours were researched in September 2026, mostly from travel guides rather than official pages, so worth a check before relying on them.
